label: Rival: being GOOD_1 in a perfection requires having it, but some had perfection is not GOOD_1
paraphrase: Rival framework commitment, unattributed, motivated by the fact/value gap (Hume's is/ought, Moore's open question) and by the objection that some actualities are bad: whatever is good in a perfection actually has it, and something actually has a perfection in which it is not good. The replacement account is that goodness is a further feature that only some actualities have. Strictly stronger than the negation of STMT-GOODNESS-IS-ACTUALITY: it keeps the direction from goodness to actuality and denies only the converse. It is not nihilism about value.
